answer: Every agent registers a beacon: a cheap signed attestation that peers continuously mirror onto the ledger. A sybil attacker must then grow a plume of real economic footprints - bonded deposits, settled trades, payment history - because verification compares against the live mirror rather than a static identity list. Fake accounts get slashed on double-attestation, and each extra identity multiplies the stake the attacker must keep posting. Forging one identity is cheap; faking a plume of many is not, since the cost scales with the size of the fake population.
